newsitem.title: USA: USDA does not see Hudson recall growing.
newsitem.headline: USDA does not see Hudson recall growing.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department said Monday it does not expect the Hudson Foods Inc ground beef recall to broaden.
"There's nothing at this moment to lead us to believe that the recall will grow," said Susan Conley, spokeswoman for USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service.

Friday, USDA announced the largest recall of U.S. ground beef products in history due to possible contamination with a deadly strain of the E. coli bacteria. Health officials blamed the bacteria for 16 cases of illness in Colorado in June.

Five million hamburger patties or 1.2 million lbs of beef processed at a Hudson plant in Columbus, Neb., over three days in June were recalled. The amount was 60 times the 20,000 lbs USDA initially said would be recalled.
Conley said a team of USDA officials arrived at the plant at 0600 EDT Monday to check records and examine sanitation and processing equipment.
"Unless we find something different, we now feel we have covered all of the distribution in those three days," Conley said, referring to Friday's recall announcement.
She said USDA would also be looking at the plants that supplied the beef to Hudson Foods. She said the department was "still pinning down" the meat suppliers.
Conley said the head of the SWAT team might report back to USDA officials in Washington later Monday but stressed the situation was unfolding.
"This is not something you can do in a couple of hours. This is something that's going to take some time," she said.
